questions.cardText:
[Zoology] What are pin feathers?
A. Immature bird feathers
B. Feather-like spikes on marine animals
C. Rigid extensions on insects for defense
Answer: A. Pin feathers, also known as blood feathers, are immature feathers on birds. They appear as small, pale protrusions filled with blood vessels. As they mature, the protective sheath surrounding them falls away, revealing fully developed feathers.
questions.de: Wie nennt man eine sich entwickelnde Vogelfeder, die noch durchblutet und von einer schützenden Hülle umgeben ist?
questions.en: What is the name for a developing bird feather that still has a blood supply and is encased in a protective sheath?

timeline.labelEn: A Late Jurassic fossil feather, once attributed to Archaeopteryx, shows feathers existed by then
timeline.labelDe: Eine Fossilfeder aus dem Oberjura, einst Archaeopteryx zugeschrieben, zeigt, dass es damals bereits Federn gab

questions.notes: Asked in reverse (definition → term). Wikipedia: a pin feather is called a blood feather only while blood still flows through it. Timeline from the Feather article's Late Jurassic fossil feather (approximate).

questions.cardText:
[Earth Science] What is a naturally occurring, solid aggregate of minerals?
A. Gemstone B. Rock C. Crystal
Answer: B. Some rocks on Earth have traveled from the Moon. These lunar meteorites are rocks that were ejected from the Moon’s surface by impact events and later landed on Earth.
questions.de: Wie nennt man in der Geologie ein natürlich vorkommendes, festes Gemenge aus Mineralen?
questions.en: In geology, what is a naturally occurring solid aggregate of minerals called?

timeline.labelEn: James Hutton publishes Theory of the Earth, helping establish modern geology
timeline.labelDe: James Hutton veröffentlicht „Theory of the Earth“ und trägt zur Begründung der modernen Geologie bei

questions.notes: Only the options removed. Timeline: Hutton's Theory of the Earth (1788 Transactions paper) per the James Hutton article.
